scope: Fission power-reactor family coverage with 2021–2026 primary-source milestones and explicitly dated international operating context; no national or global totals inferred.

families.name: Pressurized light-water reactor (PWR / VVER)
families.definition: Light water cools and moderates the core; primary coolant remains pressurized and transfers heat to a separate steam circuit.

axes.fuel_form: Solid enriched uranium oxide or mixed oxide

families.status: Commercial fleet technology, including large reactors and smaller derivative designs.
families.us_position: One of the two operating U.S. commercial power-reactor families; national fleet figures belong to the separate baseline.

examples.name: IAEA operational fleet classification
examples.achievement: The year-end operating inventory includes PWRs; the 2025 publication reports a 2024 snapshot.
examples.remaining_gate: Existing-fleet operation and new-build licensing are separate records.
examples.evidence_quote: Pressurized Light-Water Moderated and Cooled Reactor

examples.name: Vogtle Unit 4
examples.achievement: Unit 4 entered commercial service, completing the Vogtle expansion. This is delivered commercial operation, separate from advanced-reactor plans.
examples.remaining_gate: Ongoing operation; already included in the national fleet baseline.
examples.evidence_quote: Vogtle 4 entered commercial service on April 29 to wrap up the power plant’s expansion project in Waynesboro, Georgia.

families.name: Boiling light-water reactor (BWR)
families.definition: Light water cools and moderates the core and boils in the reactor to supply steam.
families.status: Commercial fleet technology; newer large and small designs use the same broad family.
families.us_position: Existing U.S. commercial fleet and BWRX-300 licensing; do not combine fleet megawatts with prospective design capacity.

examples.name: IAEA operational fleet classification
examples.achievement: The operating inventory includes BWRs; SMR describes size, not a new coolant family.
examples.remaining_gate: A particular new BWR still needs its project-specific construction and operating authorizations.
examples.evidence_quote: Boiling Light-Water Cooled and Moderated Reactor

examples.name: Clinch River Nuclear Unit 1
examples.achievement: NRC issued construction permit CPAR-2 to TVA for Clinch River Unit 1.
examples.remaining_gate: A construction permit does not establish commercial operation.
examples.evidence_quote:
DATES: The Construction Permit No. CPAR-2 was issued on September 28,
2026.

families.name: Pressurized heavy-water reactor (PHWR / CANDU)
families.definition: Heavy water moderates the core and, in conventional PHWRs, also cools pressurized fuel channels.

axes.fuel_form: Usually solid natural-uranium oxide; some designs use alternative fuel

families.us_position: International comparator; no new U.S. commercial PHWR verified in this bounded review.

examples.name: Kakrapar Unit 3
examples.achievement: The government power-allocation letter declares the 700 MW unit commercial effective June 30, 2023. This is a declared electrical-unit rating, not a net-output series.
examples.remaining_gate: Ongoing commercial operation; no contribution to U.S. deployment totals.
examples.evidence_quote: Unit 3 (700MW) of Kakrapar Atomic Power Station (2x700MW) to be commercial w.e.f. 10:00hrs of 30.06.2023.

families.name: Graphite-moderated gas-cooled reactor (GCR / AGR / Magnox)
families.definition: Graphite moderates the core and gas removes heat; historical Magnox and AGR designs are distinct from helium-cooled HTGRs.

axes.fuel_form: Solid uranium metal or oxide, depending on design

families.status: Legacy commercial fleet; distinguish remaining operating AGRs from retired Magnox units.
families.us_position: Historical and international context; no current U.S. commercial GCR build verified.

examples.name: GCR year-end fleet classification
examples.achievement: IAEA lists an operating GCR class separately from HTGR.
examples.remaining_gate: Specific unit life extensions require their own regulator decisions; no extension inferred here.

gaps: No new 2021–2026 GCR construction milestone was verified within this bounded source set.

families.name: Light-water-cooled graphite-moderated reactor (LWGR / RBMK)
families.definition: Graphite moderates the core while light water cools the fuel channels.
families.status: Legacy commercial operation abroad; not the same family as a light-water-moderated BWR.
families.us_position: International comparison; no U.S. deployment verified.

examples.name: LWGR year-end fleet classification
examples.achievement: IAEA retains an operational LWGR class, and its unit inventory identifies RBMK designs.
examples.remaining_gate: Existing operation is not evidence of a new build or modernized export design.

gaps: No new 2021–2026 LWGR construction or commercial-start milestone verified.

families.name: High-temperature gas-cooled reactor (HTGR / VHTR)
families.definition: Helium removes heat from graphite-moderated solid fuel, commonly ceramic-coated TRISO particles; VHTR is a higher-temperature development goal.

axes.fuel_form: Solid ceramic-coated particles in pebbles or prismatic blocks

families.status: Commercial demonstration abroad and active U.S. licensing/test pathways.
families.us_position: U.S. Xe-100 and pilot/test designs are tracked separately from Chinese operating proof.

examples.name: HTR-PM demonstration plant
examples.achievement: Tsinghua reports entry into commercial operation after a demonstration run. Two reactor modules share a steam turbine; the release reports2×200 MWt, not400 MWe.
examples.remaining_gate: Further replication and country-specific authorization; foreign output adds no U.S. megawatts.

examples.name: Long Mott Generating Station
examples.achievement: NRC issued a construction permit for the four-reactor facility to supply industrial steam and electricity.
examples.remaining_gate: Operating licensing and physical delivery remain separate gates.
examples.evidence_quote: ROCKVILLE, Md. — The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has issued a construction permit for the Long Mott Generating Station in Calhoun County, Texas — the first construction permit for a high-temperature gas-cooled reactor in nearly 60 years. It is the third advanced reactor construction permit the NRC has issued this year, clearing the way for Long Mott Energy to build a four-reactor facility.

families.name: Sodium-cooled fast reactor (SFR)
families.definition: Liquid sodium cools a fast-neutron core without a moderator. Fuel-cycle and breeding claims depend on the actual design and associated facilities.

axes.fuel_form: Solid metal alloy or mixed-oxide fuel, depending on design

families.status: Operating power-reactor experience abroad; new U.S. demonstration development.
families.us_position: Natrium and Aurora are prospective U.S. projects; their construction, tests and electricity claims must remain separate.

examples.name: BN-600 and BN-800 operating inventory
examples.achievement: IAEA lists BELOYARSK-3/BN-600 and BELOYARSK-4/BN-800 in its operational-reactor inventory. These are established units, not 2024 startups.
examples.remaining_gate: Separate evidence is required for a new design or breeding/fuel-recycle claim.

examples.name: Kemmerer Power Station Unit 1
examples.achievement: NRC issued construction permit CPAR-1 to US SFR Owner for the TerraPower project.
examples.remaining_gate: Construction completion and separate operating authorization remain.
examples.evidence_quote: On March 9, the NRC staff issued construction permit CPAR-1 to US SFR Owner, LLC (USO), a wholly owned subsidiary of TerraPower, LLC (TerraPower), authorizing construction of the Kemmerer Power Station, Unit 1 in Kemmerer, Wyoming. Issuance of the permit was authorized by Commission Order CLI-26-5 . Learn more .

families.name: Lead-cooled fast reactor (LFR)
families.definition: Lead or lead-bismuth eutectic removes heat from an unmoderated fast-spectrum core.

axes.fuel_form: Solid oxide or nitride fuels, depending on design

families.status: Demonstration construction and research; no commercial operation established by this source set.
families.us_position: U.S. R&D/design context; no U.S. commercial LFR build verified.

examples.name: BREST-OD-300 first concrete
examples.achievement: A GIF 2022 status presentation records construction beginning with foundation-slab concrete.
examples.remaining_gate: Completion, fuel loading and startup need current evidence. The slide’s 2026 criticality date is an old forecast, not proof it occurred.
examples.evidence_quote:
June 8 2021: Start of construction (concrete pouring of the
foundation slab)

gaps: No claim of achieved 2026 BREST criticality is made; only a 2022 forecast was located in the bounded sources.

families.name: Gas-cooled fast reactor (GFR)
families.definition: Helium cools an unmoderated fast-spectrum core, requiring refractory fuels and dedicated decay-heat safety provisions.

axes.fuel_form: Solid carbide or other refractory fuel

families.status: Concept/design and supporting research; GIF explicitly reports no operating or under-construction GFR.
families.us_position: U.S. design/R&D concepts exist; commercial deployment not verified.

examples.name: SafeG / ALLEGRO research programme
examples.achievement: GIF describes a research timeline from October 2020 through September 2024 supporting ALLEGRO; it does not report a reactor startup.
examples.remaining_gate: Demonstrator licensing, fuel qualification, construction and operation remain to be shown.
examples.evidence_quote: The SafeG project, which has a project timeline from October 2020 to September 2024

gaps: GIF states: No GFR is currently operating or under construction in the world. Its forecast power/deployment table is not an achieved milestone.

families.name: Liquid-fuel molten-salt reactor (MSR)
families.definition: Fissile material is dissolved in molten salt, which carries fuel and heat; concepts may use thermal or fast neutrons.

axes.moderator: Graphite in some thermal concepts; none in fast concepts

families.status: Experimental and development programmes; the cited U.S. milestone is fuel production, not criticality or electricity.
families.us_position: MCRE and university liquid-fuel experiments belong here; do not merge them with solid-fuel FHRs.

examples.name: Molten Chloride Reactor Experiment fuel batch
examples.achievement: DOE reported INL’s first batch of fuel salt for MCRE, a fast-spectrum salt-fueled reactor test.
examples.remaining_gate: Many further batches, reactor authorization, loading and startup were still required; the article anticipated operation in 2028.
examples.evidence_quote: Researchers at Idaho National Laboratory (INL) successfully created the first batch of fuel salt

families.name: Solid-fuel fluoride-salt-cooled high-temperature reactor (FHR)
families.definition: Molten fluoride salt cools solid TRISO fuel in a graphite-moderated core; fuel is not dissolved in the coolant.

axes.fuel_form: Solid TRISO fuel pebbles in the Kairos design

families.status: Test/demo licensing and development; separate from liquid-fuel MSRs.
families.us_position: NRC-issued Hermes 2 construction permits are an achieved licensing milestone; design ratings must name their dated basis.

examples.name: Hermes 2 construction permits
examples.achievement: NRC issued two construction permits. Its application page specifies two 35 MWth test reactors and a shared steam-powered conversion system.
examples.remaining_gate: Operation still requires authorization. A newer company 50 MWe claim must not silently replace the permitted thermal design basis.
examples.evidence_quote: issued construction permits for the Hermes 2 test reactor facility to Kairos Power LLC on November 21, 2024

gaps: NRC35 MWth-per-reactor page and company 50 MWe plant claim describe conflicting frames/design states; reconcile before assigning current built electric capacity.

families.name: Supercritical-water-cooled reactor (SCWR)
families.definition: Water above its thermodynamic critical pressure and temperature removes heat, without a liquid/steam phase change in the core circuit.
families.status: Research/design concept; the 2026 IAEA overview reports no nuclear-reactor operating experience for this coolant regime.
families.us_position: Research concept rather than a verified U.S. operating or construction project.
gaps: No 2021–2026 reactor construction or operating milestone verified. Fossil-plant supercritical steam experience is not nuclear deployment.

families.name: Heat-pipe-cooled fission reactor
families.definition: Sealed heat pipes transfer heat from solid fuel; moderator and neutron spectrum depend on the specific design.

axes.coolant: Working fluid in sealed heat pipes; design-specific

families.status: Zero-power critical experiments and prototype development; a5 MWe commercial design target is not delivered electricity.
families.us_position: The eVinci experiment reached zero-power hot criticality at NCERC in Nevada, separately from a commercial power plant or DOME campaign.

examples.name: eVinci high-temperature zero-power test
examples.achievement: DOE and Westinghouse report criticality at663°C at NCERC; the 1011°C measurement was subcritical. This is zero-power reactor-physics proof, with no grid electricity established.
examples.remaining_gate: Prototype development, facility-specific authorization, fuel loading and commercial power operation remain separate steps.
examples.evidence_quote: On September 3, 2026, the eVinci test reached criticality at 663 degrees Celsius.

historical_role_crosswalk.scope: Historical power-reactor labels, research configurations and cross-cutting applications. This is a classification crosswalk, not an exhaustive inventory of every prototype or facility.
historical_role_crosswalk.relationship_note: Coolant, moderator, neutron spectrum, fuel form, research role, power level and installation can overlap. Preserve the original authority’s database label instead of forcing every design into one flat list.

historical_labels.name: Heavy-water-moderated gas-cooled reactor (HWGCR)
historical_labels.definition: Heavy water moderates the core while gas removes heat. It is a historical hybrid of moderation and cooling choices, separate from conventional graphite-moderated GCR.
historical_labels.status: IAEA’s December 31, 2024 power-reactor table lists this historical class only under shutdown; it is not included as an operating family here.
gaps: The archive does not independently establish a recent new build or a complete inventory of research variants.

historical_labels.name: Heavy-water-moderated boiling-light-water-cooled reactor (HWLWR)
historical_labels.definition: Heavy water provides moderation while ordinary water cools the fuel and boils. Distinguish this combination from PHWR’s heavy-water coolant.
historical_labels.status: Historical power-reactor database class; IAEA lists shutdown examples rather than an operating class in the 2024 snapshot.
gaps: Do not silently rename every HWLWR design SGHWR: IAEA retains separate codes.

historical_labels.name: Steam-generating heavy-water reactor (SGHWR)
historical_labels.definition: Historical steam-generating heavy-water reactor label. It is related to the heavy-water-moderated, boiling-light-water-cooled configuration, but the IAEA database records it separately.
historical_labels.status: The December 31, 2024 IAEA table lists this class under shutdown. No current commercial deployment is asserted.
gaps: HWLWR and SGHWR overlap physically but are not interchangeable aliases in this source’s classification; design-level equivalence requires its original design record.

research_configurations.name: Open-pool research reactor
research_configurations.definition: The core is arranged in a water pool that provides cooling and shielding. Pool describes the arrangement and can overlap with TRIGA and other fuel/design classes.
research_configurations.status: An established research-reactor arrangement, not evidence of commercial electricity generation.

research_configurations.name: Tank or tank-in-pool research reactor
research_configurations.definition: The core is housed in a tank or in a tank within a pool. Vessel/arrangement labels can coexist with coolant, moderator and fuel descriptions.
research_configurations.status: Established research configurations classified separately from power-reactor families.

research_configurations.name: TRIGA research reactor
research_configurations.definition: A named research-reactor design tradition; the IAEA’s historical classification places TRIGA under the broader pool-type category. It is not a mutually exclusive coolant family.
research_configurations.status: Research/training/isotope configuration; individual facilities and fuel variants require facility-specific records.
gaps: The attempted NRC backgrounder was403-blocked. This packet does not replace a particular TRIGA facility’s fuel or licensing specification.

research_configurations.name: Aqueous homogeneous research reactor
research_configurations.definition: A water-based liquid-fuel configuration: fissile material is in solution rather than in distinct solid fuel elements. It is a subset of the broader homogeneous-liquid category, not a molten-salt reactor.
research_configurations.status: IAEA recognizes homogeneous-liquid research reactors as a historical configuration; no present commercial operating fleet is inferred.
gaps: The archived IAEA table establishes the broader homogeneous-liquid category; no named current aqueous facility, solution chemistry or electrical output was independently verified in this bounded follow-up.

research_configurations.name: Critical assembly
research_configurations.definition: A fissile-material assembly intended to sustain a controlled chain reaction at low power to investigate core geometry and composition. Criticality alone establishes no electric generation.
research_configurations.status: Research/physics-test role; it may exercise material and temperature conditions relevant to a future power reactor.

research_configurations.name: Subcritical assembly
research_configurations.definition: An assembly with effective multiplication below one. With an external neutron source its neutrons can be multiplied, while the assembly remains below the self-sustaining critical condition.
research_configurations.status: Research/training or source-driven configuration; do not report subcritical measurements as achieved criticality.

cross_cutting_axes.name: Naval and marine propulsion
cross_cutting_axes.definition: A propulsion/application label, to be combined with a reactor’s actual coolant, moderator, spectrum and fuel design. It is not a new mutually exclusive fission family.
cross_cutting_axes.status: Application axis; no national naval fleet census or classified design inference is attempted.
gaps: The archived IAEA taxonomy includes ship-propulsion applications but does not enumerate naval fleets.

cross_cutting_axes.name: Space fission systems
cross_cutting_axes.definition: Space describes the mission and environment. A space reactor still has a physical reactor family; radioisotope power sources are not fission reactors simply because both are nuclear.
cross_cutting_axes.status: Application axis; no recent mission milestone or comprehensive space-reactor inventory verified in this packet.
gaps: A dedicated NASA/DOE space-fission source remains needed before adding mission-specific power or deployment statistics.

cross_cutting_axes.name: Floating nuclear installation
cross_cutting_axes.definition: Floating describes siting or plant installation, not a distinct coolant/moderator/neutron-spectrum family. A floating design must retain its actual reactor technology label.
cross_cutting_axes.status: Installation axis; the IAEA technology survey includes floating applications across concepts.

cross_cutting_axes.name: Large reactor, SMR and microreactor
cross_cutting_axes.definition: Size and modular construction describe power or delivery scale. Water, gas, salt, liquid-metal and heat-pipe concepts can occupy different size classes.
cross_cutting_axes.status: Scale axis; thresholds and electrical/thermal units must be stated from the relevant authority.

cross_cutting_axes.name: Fuel composition and fuel cycle
cross_cutting_axes.definition: Uranium, plutonium and thorium refer to fuel/material choices; open or closed cycles describe material management. These do not by themselves identify a coolant/moderator family.
cross_cutting_axes.status: Fuel and lifecycle axes; fuel-production milestones do not prove reactor operation or recycling at commercial scale.

cross_cutting_axes.name: Power, heat, isotope production and research
cross_cutting_axes.definition: Application and research roles can overlap the same reactor physics. Electricity, heat, neutron production and criticality are distinct output/achievement frames.
cross_cutting_axes.status: Role axis; preserve separate thermal, electrical and research statistics.

evidence.quote: Heavy-Water Moderated, Boiling Light-Water Cooled Reactor
pool type reactors, tank type reactors or tank-in-pool type reactors

gaps: No complete inventory of all historical prototypes, pulse devices, irradiation facilities, naval reactors or space experiments is claimed.
The 2006 research-reactor report is used for configuration nomenclature, not for current facility counts; the 2023 compendium is used for definitions.
No source examined here establishes that HWLWR and SGHWR are exact interchangeable database aliases. Their physical overlap is described without merging the authority’s separate labels.
A dedicated primary source for each named current aqueous or space facility remains required before publishing facility-level power, dates or status.
